role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint

first_impression.what_i_think_it_is: A stateless MCP server with a catalog of deterministic CRE calculators that my agent graph can call instead of doing math in the model.
first_impression.why: The connectors README and llms.txt both give a streamable HTTP MCP endpoint with no key, and the tools are read-only. That is the minimum an agent framework needs.

onboarding.path_followed: connectors README: remote MCP at https://api.factlot.com/mcp; replayed what a framework's MCP adapter does: initialize, tools/list, tools/call. The framework step itself (LangGraph adapter) not run.
stuck_points: Nothing in the materials says anything about agent-framework specifics (schema dialect, structured output). I inspected tools/list myself: 42 tools, draft-07 schemas, 14 oneOf and 40 pattern keywords, no $ref, no outputSchema on any tool.

Successful tool results carry both a JSON string in a text content item and a structuredContent object (value, formula, steps, warnings, provenance), but tools/list declares no outputSchema for any tool; error results carry only the text item.
not_tested: Loading the 42 tool definitions into LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK or CrewAI (strict-mode schema compatibility with oneOf and long regex patterns is unknown)
Concurrency under the 60-per-minute limit with several graph branches

clear: Stateless Streamable HTTP, free tier at 60 a minute per address (site-llms.txt)
Read-only annotations on every tool (observed in tools/list)
Calculator results carry steps, warnings and a formula ID that I can drop into a credit memo
unclear_or_unconvincing: Per-address rate limit shared by every agent behind one NAT; the docs do not say what happens to a graph that fans out calls
No statement about framework compatibility or tested versions in the materials
missing_proof: A tested example for at least one agent framework
Latency distribution (my calls took 0.5 to 1.8 s)
An error-code table for HTTP 429 and its Retry-After on the free tier (the docs mention 429 for keyed limits only)
marketing.headline_for_my_role: A free, stateless MCP tool server whose hotel KPIs, debt sizing and stress tables your agent graph can call and cite instead of computing in-context.
where_i_would_look_for_it: The MCP Registry and framework tool catalogs

output_quality.error_handling: Errors are MCP isError results with a readable message, so a graph can retry. Validation stops at the first layer: schema errors hide logic errors until the next call. The rooms_sold error carries an empty issues array.

what_worked: Hotel KPIs and sizing reproduced exactly
isError results rather than transport failures; successful results include structuredContent, so no string parsing
Stateless, no key: trivial for a graph node
Stress table in one call
problems: Not tested: whether 14 oneOf and 40 pattern keywords load into strict-schema frameworks (tools/list)
Logic errors (rooms_sold above capacity) have an empty issues array (calc_hotel_metrics call)
No documented behaviour for 429 on the free tier
pay_for_what: Nothing now; $49 for the 600 per minute tier if my graph fans out, provided there is an SLA, which the terms say is not guaranteed.
must_have_lever: A tested framework recipe (LangGraph and OpenAI Agents SDK) with schema-compatible tool definitions and a documented 429 and retry policy.
honest_reaction: The tools are what a lender's agent graph wants: deterministic, cited, read-only. I could not tell from the docs whether my framework will swallow 42 oneOf-heavy schemas, and that is the first thing I would check. The math reproduced.
